name: UP Krishi Yantra Subsidy Yojana
description: Financial subsidy up to 50% on agricultural implements including rotavators, happy seeders, laser land levelers, and power sprayers for farmers of Uttar Pradesh.
benefits: Direct bank subsidy of 40% - 50% (up to ₹1,00,000) on approved agricultural machinery through UP Agriculture portal e-lottery token system.
eligibility: Registered farmer on upagriculture.com portal with valid Farmer ID (Kisan Panjikaran)
Resident of Uttar Pradesh with operational cultivable land in UP
One implement per farmer per category once in 3 years
requiredDocuments: Bank Passbook linked to DBT account
applicationProcess: Step 1: Book online token on upagriculture.com during open booking window.
Step 2: Deposit security token money within 3 working days at Union Bank of India or online.
Step 3: Upload bill and serial number of machinery purchased from registered dealer.
Step 4: Physical verification by District Agriculture Officer (DAO).
Step 5: Direct subsidy credit to bank account via DBT.
department: Department of Agriculture, Govt. of Uttar Pradesh

name: Mukhyamantri Khet Suraksha Yojana
description: Solar fencing subsidy scheme to safeguard standing crops from stray animals and wild boars without causing harm to animals.
benefits: 60% subsidy (up to ₹1,43,000 per hectare) for installing solar-powered low voltage pulsating fences around cultivable fields.
eligibility: Individual farmers or farmer groups in Uttar Pradesh suffering crop depredation from stray animals
Minimum 1 hectare contiguous land holding for group application
requiredDocuments: Field boundary map certified by Lekhpal
applicationProcess: Step 1: Submit application on UP Agriculture Portal under Solar Fencing module.
Step 2: On-site verification of perimeter length by agriculture supervisor.
Step 3: Installation of certified solar fence unit by empanelled vendor.
Step 4: Joint inspection and subsidy release.
department: Department of Agriculture, Govt. of Uttar Pradesh

name: Bihar Rajya Fasal Sahayata Yojana (BRFSY)
description: Zero-premium crop assistance scheme providing direct compensation to both landowning and tenant farmers of Bihar in case of crop yield loss.
benefits: ₹7,500/hectare for yield loss up to 20%; ₹10,000/hectare for yield loss greater than 20%. Completely free registration with zero premium required from farmers.
eligibility: All resident farmers of Bihar (both Ryot / Landowners and Non-Ryot / Sharecroppers)
Must have cultivated notified crops (Paddy, Maize, Wheat, Gram, Mustard) in notified Gram Panchayat
requiredDocuments: Bihar Farmer Registration Number (DBT Bihar Portal)
Land Possession Certificate (LPC) / Revenue Receipt (for Ryot)
Self-declaration certificate verified by Ward Member / PACS Chairman (for Non-Ryot)
applicationProcess: Step 1: Apply online on state cooperative portal (pacsonline.bih.nic.in).
Step 2: Upload land documents and crop declaration photos.
Step 3: Crop Cutting Experiment (CCE) based gram panchayat yield loss assessment.
Step 4: Automatic direct compensation payout to eligible farmers' bank accounts.
department: Department of Co-operative, Govt. of Bihar

name: Bihar Diesel Anudan Yojana
description: Financial subsidy for diesel irrigation to protect standing crops during dry spells and drought-like weather conditions in Bihar.
benefits: ₹75 per liter of diesel (up to ₹750 per acre per irrigation cycle, maximum 3 irrigations for Paddy and 4 for Pulses/Oilseeds).
eligibility: All registered farmers of Bihar owning or leasing land affected by monsoon delays or dry spells
Diesel must be purchased from authorized petrol pumps with valid computerized invoice
requiredDocuments: Computerized Diesel Purchase Receipt (with 13-digit registration no.)
applicationProcess: Step 1: Apply on dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in under Diesel Anudan.
Step 2: Upload scanned copy of computerized diesel petrol pump invoice.
Step 3: Verification by Panchayat Agriculture Coordinator (AC) within 7 days.
Step 4: Immediate DBT payment directly to farmer's bank account.
department: Department of Agriculture, Govt. of Bihar

name: Namo Shetkari Mahasanman Nidhi Yojana
description: Additional annual financial assistance of ₹6,000 by the Government of Maharashtra to all PM-KISAN beneficiary farmers in the state.
benefits: ₹6,000/year in 3 equal installments of ₹2,000 (combining with PM-KISAN to give Maharashtra farmers a total of ₹12,000 annually).
eligibility: All active beneficiaries of PM-KISAN in the state of Maharashtra
Must have completed Aadhaar authentication and land record linking in Mahadbt portal
requiredDocuments: Bank Account linked with Aadhaar NPCI mapper
applicationProcess: Step 1: Automatic onboarding for all verified PM-KISAN beneficiaries in Maharashtra.
Step 2: Status check and eKYC update on mahadbt.maharashtra.gov.in.
Step 3: Direct deposit of ₹2,000 every 4 months alongside central PM-KISAN release.

name: Magel Tyala Shettale (Farm Pond On Demand Scheme)
description: Providing financial grants to farmers of Maharashtra to dig individual farm ponds for harvesting rainwater and drought proofing.
benefits: Direct grant up to ₹75,000 for standard farm pond excavation + additional ₹1,00,000 subsidy for plastic lining to prevent seepage.
eligibility: Farmers owning minimum 0.60 hectare (1.5 acres) cultivable land in Maharashtra
Land must be physically suitable for watershed and water storage
applicationProcess: Step 1: Register on MahaDBT Farmer Portal.
Step 2: Select 'Magel Tyala Shettale' under Irrigation Infrastructure.
Step 3: Technical drawing and approval by Taluka Agriculture Officer (TAO).
Step 4: Excavation and geo-tagged photographic inspection.
Step 5: Direct subsidy disbursement into DBT account.

name: Punjab Crop Residue Management (CRM) Subsidy
description: Subsidized distribution of in-situ crop residue management machinery (Super SMS, Happy Seeder, Smart Seeder, Paddy Straw Chopper, Mulcher) to prevent stubble burning.
benefits: 50% individual subsidy for farmers and 80% subsidy for Custom Hiring Centers (CHCs) and Cooperatives on designated crop residue management machines.
eligibility: Cultivators in Punjab having cultivable paddy land
Individual farmers, registered Cooperative Societies, Panchayats, and FPOs
applicationProcess: Step 1: Apply on agrimachinerypb.com portal with Aadhaar and tractor details.
Step 2: Department approves eligible applicants via transparent computerized lottery.
Step 3: Purchase machinery from empanelled manufacturers with unique chassis number.
Step 4: Physical geo-tagged inspection by agriculture team.
Step 5: DBT subsidy release into bank account.
department: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Govt. of Punjab

name: Pani Bachao, Paisa Kamao (PBPK) Scheme
description: Direct financial incentive to Punjab farmers for conserving groundwater and electricity by using less power on agricultural tube wells.
benefits: ₹4.00 per kilowatt-hour (kWh) electricity saved against baseline quota credited directly to the farmer's bank account every month.
eligibility: Farmers having operational agricultural electricity tube well connections in notified feeder blocks of Punjab
requiredDocuments: PSPCL (Punjab State Power Corp) Consumer Account Number
applicationProcess: Step 1: Voluntary enrollment at local PSPCL sub-division or via Kisan Sathi portal.
Step 2: Free installation of automated digital energy meter on agriculture connection.
Step 3: Baseline power quota assigned based on land area.
Step 4: Monthly savings calculated and direct cash incentive credited to bank.

name: Mera Pani Meri Virasat Yojana
description: Financial incentive to Haryana farmers who switch from water-guzzling paddy to alternative crops such as Maize, Cotton, Pulses, Millets, and Horticulture.
benefits: ₹7,000 per acre direct financial assistance for every acre shifted away from paddy cultivation to designated alternate crops or left fallow for agroforestry.
eligibility: Farmers registered on Meri Fasal Mera Byora (MFMB) portal of Haryana who cultivated paddy in the preceding year
applicationProcess: Step 1: Register crop switching details on fasal.haryana.gov.in portal.
Step 2: Satellite imagery and field verification by Revenue & Agriculture staff.
Step 3: Verification of alternate crop establishment.
Step 4: Two-installment DBT payout (₹2,000 on verification + ₹5,000 post flowering).
department: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Haryana

name: Bhavantar Bharpayee Yojana (BBY)
description: Price deficit compensation scheme protecting Haryana horticulture and vegetable growers from market price crashes below protected base prices.
benefits: Compensation for the difference between the government fixed benchmark price and the actual mandi sale price for 21 notified vegetable & fruit crops.
eligibility: Horticulture growers of Haryana cultivating notified vegetables (Tomato, Onion, Potato, Cauliflower, Carrot, etc.) and registered on MFMB
requiredDocuments: Mandi J-Form (Sale Receipt from Haryana Mandi)
applicationProcess: Step 1: Register crop sowing on MFMB during the notified window.
Step 2: Sell produce at any notified APMC mandi in Haryana and obtain computerized J-Form.
Step 3: Automatic deficit calculation against minimum benchmark price.
Step 4: Direct payout credited into farmer's account within 15 days.

name: Krishi Bhagya Yojana
description: Integrated package for rainfed farmers in Karnataka including polythene-lined farm ponds, diesel/solar pumps, and micro-irrigation sets for protective irrigation.
benefits: 80% to 90% subsidy for SC/ST farmers; 50% to 80% subsidy for General farmers on complete farm pond construction and polythene lining unit.
eligibility: Farmers owning land in rainfed and drought-prone taluks of Karnataka
Registered on FRUITS (Farmer Registration and Unified Beneficiary Information System) portal
applicationProcess: Step 1: Apply via FRUITS portal or Raitha Samparka Kendra (RSK).
Step 2: Pre-inspection and feasibility certification by Assistant Director of Agriculture.
Step 3: Excavation of farm pond and laying of 500-micron UV stabilized sheet.
Step 4: Post-inspection and direct DBT transfer of subsidy.
department: Department of Agriculture, Govt. of Karnataka

name: YSR Rythu Bharosa
description: Comprehensive input assistance scheme offering ₹13,500 per year to landowning farmer families and ₹13,500 to landless SC/ST/BC/Minority tenant farmer families.
benefits: ₹13,500 per farmer family annually in 3 installments (₹7,500 in May before sowing, ₹4,000 in October for harvest/Rabi, ₹2,000 in January on Sankranti).
eligibility: All farmer families cultivating land in Andhra Pradesh
Eligible tenant farmers possessing valid Crop Cultivator Rights Cards (CCRC)
requiredDocuments: Crop Cultivator Rights Card (CCRC) for tenant farmers
applicationProcess: Step 1: Village Agriculture Assistant (VAA) at Rythu Bharosa Kendra (RBK) conducts door-to-door enumeration.
Step 2: Social audit list displayed at village secretariat.
Step 3: Direct biometric authentication and immediate DBT payout.
department: Agriculture & Cooperation Department, Govt. of Andhra Pradesh

name: Mukhyamantri Kisan Kalyan Yojana
description: State top-up scheme providing additional ₹6,000 annually in 3 installments to all eligible PM-KISAN beneficiary farmers in Madhya Pradesh.
benefits: ₹6,000/year directly credited in 3 equal installments of ₹2,000 to augment farmer household income.
eligibility: Resident farmers of Madhya Pradesh enrolled and receiving PM-KISAN benefits
Cultivable land record updated on MP Bhulekh portal
applicationProcess: Step 1: Automatic verification via SAARA (Smart Application for Agricultural Revenue Administration) portal.
Step 2: Patwari field verification of land status.
Step 3: Approval by Tehsildar and automated DBT release.
department: Revenue and Agriculture Department, Govt. of Madhya Pradesh

name: Rajasthan Tarbandi Yojana
description: Subsidy for barbed wire boundary fencing to protect crops from stray cattle, nilgai, and wild animals in agricultural fields across Rajasthan.
benefits: 50% to 60% subsidy (up to ₹48,000 for individual farmers and up to ₹56,000 for small/marginal farmers) for 400 running meters of barbed wire fencing.
eligibility: Individual farmers having minimum 1.5 hectares of cultivable land or group of farmers having minimum 5 hectares in Rajasthan
requiredDocuments: Bank Passbook linked to Jan Aadhaar
applicationProcess: Step 1: Apply online on RajKisan Sathi portal (rajkisan.rajasthan.gov.in).
Step 2: Pre-verification by Agriculture Supervisor.
Step 3: Complete barbed wire fencing installation as per standards.
Step 4: Post-verification and geo-tagged inspection.
Step 5: Direct subsidy deposit into Jan Aadhaar bank account.
department: Department of Agriculture, Govt. of Rajasthan

name: Kalaignar All Village Integrated Agriculture Development Programme
description: Converting fallow lands into cultivable land with distribution of high quality seed kits, saplings, micro-irrigation, and solar pumps in Tamil Nadu village panchayats.
benefits: Free agricultural input kits containing quality seeds, fruit saplings, bio-fertilizers, battery sprayers (50% subsidy), and farm toolkits for rural farmers.
eligibility: Farmers residing in selected village panchayats of Tamil Nadu enrolled in Uzhavan App
applicationProcess: Step 1: Register through the Uzhavan App or Village Agricultural Extension Centre (AEC).
Step 2: Select eligible component (Seed Kit, Orchard Planting, Sprayer).
Step 3: Collection from local Agricultural Extension Centre upon SMS intimation.
department: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Tamil Nadu

name: Gujarat Saat Pagla Khedut Kalyanna Yojana
description: Seven-step comprehensive farmer welfare package in Gujarat covering small storage godowns, indigenous cow maintenance, toolkits, and crop protection.
benefits: Subsidies up to ₹30,000 for farm godown construction; ₹900/month (₹10,800/yr) for maintaining indigenous cows; 75% subsidy on drum toolkits for natural farming.
eligibility: Farmers registered on i-Khedut portal of Gujarat with active 7/12 land records
applicationProcess: Step 1: Apply on ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in portal during open application window.
Step 2: Scrutiny by District Agriculture Office.
Step 3: Construction / purchase as per guidelines.
Step 4: Physical inspection and direct DBT payment.
department: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare & Co-operation Dept, Gujarat

name: Krishak Bandhu (Natun) Scheme
description: Flagship scheme of West Bengal providing assured financial assistance for agricultural inputs and ₹2,00,000 death benefit insurance for farmer families.
benefits: ₹10,000 per year (for 1 or more acre land) in two equal installments (Kharif & Rabi); pro-rata assistance for smaller lands (min ₹4,000/yr) + ₹2 Lakh death insurance.
eligibility: All farmers and recorded Bhagchasi (Sharecroppers) residing in West Bengal aged 18 to 60 years
applicationProcess: Step 1: Apply at Duare Sarkar camp or Assistant Director of Agriculture (ADA) office.
Step 2: Issue of Krishak Bandhu digital smart card with unique KB-ID.
Step 3: Direct deposit of Kharif installment in June and Rabi installment in November.
department: Department of Agriculture, Govt. of West Bengal
